evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The start page lists title, date and time, EUR price and "<n> seats left" (start.jpg; TastingsPage.tsx:50-65). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingsPage.tsx:71). The form has Name, Email and Guests fields and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:102-143). The server enforces the seat limit and returns errors per field (app.ts:63-79; bookings.ts:80-81), and these are shown next to the field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the "Booking confirmed" heading, the tasting, guests, total and reference (confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, with the password taken from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:8; staff.ts:94-108). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, plus a Cancel button that frees seats (staff.jpg; staff.ts:124-143). The app is built with React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. The scripts are npm build and npm start, and PORT defaults to 3000 (index.ts:6). There is a fully booked state (TastingsPage.tsx:44-48, BookingPage.tsx:45-58) and a responsive grid. One small wording difference: with one seat left the page shows "1 seat left" (format.ts:20), not the literal "1 seats left" pattern from the brief.
evidence.correctness: createBooking is synchronous: it checks and pushes in one tick (bookings.ts:79-93), so concurrent requests cannot oversell. A test fires 20 bookings at once (bookings.test.ts:80-91). The zod schema is shared by client and server. It rejects 0, 9, 2.5, NaN, a string "3", whitespace-only names, control characters and overlong fields (booking.ts:4-22; booking.test.ts). A 409 response names the seats left (app.ts:25-28,78). Cancelling splices the booking out, so its seats are freed, and a cancelled reference returns 404. If persisting fails, the in-memory change is rolled back (bookings.ts:86-104), and file writes are atomic temp-then-rename writes (bookings.ts:41-57). Dates are formatted in UTC so the day does not shift (format.ts:1-13). Small gap: the bookings file is loaded without validating its shape (bookings.ts:34-39).
evidence.security: The password is compared in constant time with timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests (staff.ts:26-34). The session is regenerated on sign-in (staff.ts:103), the cookie is httpOnly, SameSite=lax and secure:auto (staff.ts:81), the secret is random per process (staff.ts:77), and the server enforces both an idle limit and an absolute session lifetime (staff.ts:49-56). Failed sign-ins are rate limited (staff.ts:85-92). Other protections: helmet, a 10 kB JSON limit, a generic 500 with no stack leak (app.ts:48-49,104-121), Cache-Control no-store on staff routes, and a public confirmation endpoint that omits name and email (app.ts:30-39). React escapes all output. There are no secrets in the code. MemoryStore is acknowledged as a single-process shortcut (staff.ts:74).
evidence.code_quality: The code is small and clearly split into shared (schema, catalogue), server (app, store, staff router) and client (pages, components, api, format) modules. Naming is clear, and the API client uses a typed discriminated union (api.ts:27-41). Errors are handled at each layer. There is little duplication; the load-tastings effect is repeated in two pages, which is a minor point. TypeScript is strict throughout.
evidence.tests: The suite uses Vitest and supertest. It covers the catalogue, schema boundaries, the store (seat limit, persistence, rollback, concurrency, cancel), the guest API (201, 400 per field, 404, 409 messages, malformed JSON, 413, generic 500, confirmation without personal data), the staff API (cookie flags, Secure behind a proxy, wrong password, 503, 401, session fixation, rate limit, idle and absolute expiry, sign-out, grouping, cancel freeing seats) and SPA fallback. There are no React component tests and no end-to-end tests, so the visible labels and texts ("Book <title>", the field-level error display, the confirmation page) are not tested automatically.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg and staff.jpg show a coherent winery look: a wine-red header, a cream background, serif headings, card layout and clear CTAs. The invalid email gets a red-tinted field and an inline message (form.jpg). The confirmation card is clear and reminds the guest to keep the reference. The staff view shows a "x of y seats booked" summary and "No bookings yet" for empty tastings. Weaknesses: Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation and no success message (StaffPage.tsx:109-114,164-170), and the design is fairly plain, with no imagery or winery character beyond the colours.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked with htmlFor/id (Field.tsx:16). Errors use role=alert and are linked through aria-invalid and aria-describedby (Field.tsx:21; BookingPage.tsx:108-109). The page uses semantic dl/dt/dd with sr-only terms (TastingsPage.tsx:50-65), sets lang=en, has touch targets of at least 44px (min-h-11) and focus-visible outlines on inputs and links. The palette contrast appears adequate. Gaps: focus is not moved or announced on route changes, for example to the confirmation heading. The multiple "Cancel" buttons have no booking-specific accessible name (StaffPage.tsx:164-170). The guests hint is not linked through aria-describedby (BookingPage.tsx:135).
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are mainstream and fit the brief (express, express-session, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, tailwind). helmet and express-rate-limit add a little scope, but they are justified. Total code is a few hundred lines. Two pieces go beyond the brief's need: the idle and absolute session-lifetime machinery, and the fsync-based atomic file persistence.
evidence.maintainability: OpenSpec specs document the behaviour well (openspec/specs/*), and package-lock.json is present. However, the repository has no README, so setup, the STAFF_PASSWORD, BOOKINGS_FILE and TRUST_PROXY_HOPS variables, the data/ directory and the run commands are documented nowhere except in code and specs. There is no CI configuration, no ADRs, no staff manual and no release or changelog approach (version 0.1.0 is unused). Node is only constrained by engines ">=22", with no .nvmrc. Built dist/ and .playwright-mcp artefacts were delivered even though they are gitignored.

unmet_requirements: Minor wording deviation: one remaining seat is shown as "1 seat left" (format.ts:20) rather than the literal "<n> seats left" pattern
strengths: Server-side booking logic is solid: shared zod validation, a synchronous seat check that cannot oversell under concurrent requests, rollback when persistence fails, and per-field errors including a 409 that names the seats left (bookings.ts:79-93, app.ts:57-80)
Strong staff security: constant-time password comparison, session regeneration, httpOnly/SameSite cookies, idle and absolute session expiry, rate limiting, helmet and no-store (staff.ts)
Thorough API and store tests plus a coherent, polished winery visual design with clear error, success and fully booked states (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, staff.jpg)
issues: No README, CI pipeline, ADRs, staff guide or release approach: setup, environment variables (STAFF_PASSWORD, BOOKINGS_FILE, TRUST_PROXY_HOPS) and data-file location are documented only in specs and code
Staff Cancel deletes a booking at once, with no confirmation, no success feedback and no booking-specific accessible name (StaffPage.tsx:109-114,164-170)
No client component or end-to-end tests, so the visible labels, field-level error rendering and confirmation page are not tested automatically; focus is also not managed on route changes
review.verdict: The app meets the brief functionally, with correct seat handling, robust staff security, good server tests and a polished, coherent winery design. Before handing it over, the repository needs a README and CI, the staff cancel action needs a confirmation step, and the UI needs some automated tests.
